primary_claim: LLM agents (Claude 3.7, Gemini 2.5 Pro, o3) playing Pokémon Red are severely limited by poor vision, weak spatial/navigation reasoning, and an inability to update beliefs against contradicting evidence, with progress highly dependent on scaffold engineering (overlays, labeling tools, checkpoints) rather than raw model capability.
stated_future_work: test whether Gemini can distinguish the cuttable tree from regular trees
introduce a 'Navigation Claude' fed an exploration map and goal, tasked solely with giving navigation advice
try brute-force fixes like full context wipes every ~1000 steps if a model hasn't left a location, to break hallucination loops
curious whether LLMs would do better on later-generation Pokemon games
limitations_stated: the scaffold is not fully identical across models; technical differences were needed to format data the way each model prefers
observations are informal and anecdotal rather than a systematic controlled study
author has not yet tested whether Gemini can distinguish the cuttable tree
running these experiments is costly (~$30 per 2000 steps), limiting how much experimentation was done
quote: It takes only the briefest amount of watching to convince yourself that the models can barely see what's going on, if at all.
